brief: The Market Ear opens with three indicators past peak: Trump's approval rating sliding to a declining baseline rather than mean-reverting as in his first term, Anthropic's annualized revenue run rate growth slowing sharply after rising from about $10bn in January to $74bn by July 24 but only to $76.8bn by September 24 (about 4% growth in two months versus a sevenfold rise over the prior seven months), and the share of US adults who drink alcohol falling to 54%, the lowest since Gallup began asking almost 90 years ago. The rest is a 15-chart roundup reporting disparate data with no single thesis: CCC-rated credit spreads above 1,000bps and at a record ratio to high-yield; Oracle's five-year CDS near record highs around 261bps, implying roughly 20% five-year default risk; France and NVDA CDS trading at a similar level; US banks the most oversold versus the market since 1993; Taiwan and Korea now half the MXAPJ index weight, displacing China; EM equities starting to outperform US equities; buyback authorizations at $1.1 trillion YTD, over 20% ahead of last year; and hedge fund long/short positioning at its lowest in a year.
